content: This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to you outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are uncommon. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States or Canada and experience side effects, contact your doctor for medical advice. Precautions: Before starting this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to conjugated estrogens, bazedoxifene, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Avoid smoking or using tobacco while on this medication. Notify your doctor if you have recently undergone surgery, are planning surgery, or will be immobile for an extended period (e.g., during a long flight), as these conditions can increase your risk of blood clots, especially when taking estrogen products. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen or protective clothing when outdoors. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses. This medication must not be used during pregnancy. Estrogens can pass into breast milk and may reduce its quality and quantity. It is unknown if bazedoxifene passes into breast milk, so breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., metyrapone test, blood clotting tests, thyroid tests), potentially causing inaccurate results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Regular Monitoring: Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Lifestyle Changes: Lifestyle changes such as reducing stress, eating a low-fat and low-salt diet, losing weight if overweight, exercising regularly, and quitting smoking can help. To promote healthy bones, engage in weight-bearing exercises, avoid smoking, limit alcohol consumption, and eat a balanced diet rich in calcium and vitamin D. Keeping your mind active with mental exercises like reading or solving puzzles may help prevent dementia. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication in its original packaging at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Once the foil pouch is opened, the U.S. product expires after 60 days, and the Canadian product expires after 45 days. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
